message.content:
Below are two ways to spin‑up a **Google Compute Engine** virtual machine that has one **NVIDIA RTX A6000** GPU attached and boots from **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> ⚠️ *Prerequisites*  
> • You must already have a project enabled for Compute Engine and have sufficient quotas for GPUs in your region (`nvidia-a6000`).  
> • Your account/service‑account must hold at least the following roles:  
>   - `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1`  
>   - `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser`  
>   - `roles/resourcemanager.projectIamAdmin` (if you’re assigning custom service accounts)  

---

## 1️⃣ Create the instance with the **gcloud CLI**

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

PROJECT="YOUR_PROJECT_ID"
ZONE="us-central1-b"          # pick a zone that supports RTX A6000
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-demo"

# Machine type – choose something that fits your CPU/memory budget
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-highmem-16"

# Image family & project for Ubuntu 20.04 LTS
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

# Service account (optional)
SERVICE_ACCOUNT="${PROJECT}@${PROJECT}.iam.gserviceaccount.com"

# Scopes – allow full control of Compute resources + logging
SCOPES=("https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform")

echo "Creating $INSTANCE_NAME …"

gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --boot-disk-size=50GB \
  --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \
  --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \
  --scopes="$(IFS=',' ; echo "${SCOPES[*]}")" \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \     # optional init script
  --tags=http-server,https-server \
  --network-interface network-tier=PREMIUM,subnet=${ZONE}-default \
  --no-restart-on-failure \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --reservation-affinity=any \
  --guest-cpus=auto \
  --enable-stackdriver-monitoring \
  --enable-stackdriver-trace \
  --service-account="$SERVICE_ACCOUNT" \
  --access-config-name="External NAT" \
  --labels env=demo,gpu=true \
  --accelerators count=1,type=nvidia-a6000 \
  --preemptible=false

echo "Instance created successfully."
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | Determines vCPU / RAM. Pick a type that meets your workload’s memory requirements. |
| `--accelerators` | Attaches the requested GPU(s); here `count=1,type=nvidia-a6000`. |
| `--image-family`, `--image-project` | Boots from the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the root volume (you can increase if needed). |
| `--service-account` | Optional SA that runs the VM. |
| `--scopes` | Grants OAuth scopes; `"cloud-platform"` gives broad access. |

After running the script, SSH into the instance and install CUDA drivers if you plan to run GPU workloads:

```bash
sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y
wget https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/repos/ubuntu2004/x86_64/cuda-keyring.deb
sudo dpkg -i cuda-keyring.deb
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y cuda-drivers
```

---

## 2️⃣ Call the **REST API directly** (curl)

If you prefer to hit the Compute Engine API yourself, here's a minimal POST payload that creates the same kind of instance.

```bash
API_ENDPOINT="https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/${PROJECT}/zones/${ZONE}/instances"
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)

cat <<EOF >instance.json
{
  "name": "${INSTANCE_NAME}",
  "machineType": "projects/${PROJECT}/zones/${ZONE}/machineTypes/${MACHINE_TYPE}",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "diskSizeGb": 50,
        "sourceImageFamily": "${IMAGE_FAMILY}",
        "sourceImageProject": "${IMAGE_PROJECT}"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [{
    "networkTier":"PREMIUM",
    "subNetwork":"global/networks/default",
    "accessConfigs":[{"kind":"compute#accessConfig","name":"External NAT"}]
  }],
  "scheduling": {"automaticRestart":true,"onHostMaintenance":"MIGRATE"},
  "serviceAccounts":[{
    "email":"${SERVICE_ACCOUNT}",
    "scopes":["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
  }],
  "accelerators":[
    { "deviceCount":"1", "acceleratorType":"projects/${PROJECT}/locations/${ZONE}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a6000"}
  ]
}
EOF

curl -X POST "${API_ENDPOINT}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json
```

#### Notes on the JSON fields

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|--------|
| `machineType` | Full resource path including project and zone. |
| `accellerators.deviceCount` | Number of GPUs. |
| `accellerators.acceleratorType` | Path to the specific GPU SKU (`nvidia-a6000`). |
| `disks.initializeParams.sourceImageFamily/sourceImageProject` | Pulls the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image automatically. |
| `serviceAccounts.scopes` | Gives the VM permission to act across all APIs. |

Once the response shows `"status":"RUNNING"`, the VM is ready. Connect via SSH:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh "${INSTANCE_NAME}" --zone="${ZONE}"
```

And again install CUDA drivers inside the VM if required.

---

## Quick Checklist

| ✅ Item | How to verify |
|---|---|
| Project ID | `gcloud projects list` |
| Zone supports RTX A6000 | Check [GPU availability](https://cloud.google.com/gcp-resource-manager/docs/quota-overview) |
| Quotas allocated | `gcloud compute regions describe us-central1` → look under “Accelerator” |
| Billing enabled | Console → Billing |
| Proper IAM role | `gcloud projects get-iam-policy YOUR_PROJECT_ID` |

That’s everything you need to launch a Compute Engine instance equipped with an RTX A6000 GPU and running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS! 🚀
